metaDescription: Six 44-inch tow-behind lawn sweepers compared on hopper size, brush ratio, folding design and upkeep, so you can pick one that fits your tractor and lot.
expertTake: The Agri-Fab 44-inch with its 28 cu ft flow-through bag and published 5.6 to 1 brush ratio is the best pick, and the Garvee 44-inch is the value-minded alternative if you want a folding frame. Anyone with a small lot or a very light tractor should drop to a 42 inch sweeper with a smaller bag.
introParagraphs: A 44 inch tow-behind sweeper sits in the middle of the width range. It cuts passes compared with narrower units, yet still fits most garden gates and lane widths once you account for the frame outside the brush path.

These machines are ground driven, so the wheels spin the brushes and a tractor, zero-turn or ATV supplies the pull. Brush speed, hopper design and frame stiffness decide how well one performs, far more than the width printed on the box.

products.name: Agri-Fab 44-Inch Tow Sweeper 28 cu ft Flow-Through
products.description:
The Agri-Fab is the only sweeper here that publishes a brush-to-wheel ratio, 5.6 to 1, which means the brushes turn 5.6 times for every wheel turn. That ratio is what keeps pickup working at ordinary mower speeds, and it is paired with a 28 cu ft flow-through bag that fills from back to front.

Its tradeoff is size. A 28 cu ft bag is the largest in the group, tied with the CuisinAid, and it asks more of the tow vehicle than the 26 cu ft Garvee when full.

Ownership favors it. Agri-Fab is an established maker of ground-driven tractor attachments, so manuals and replacement bags and brushes are easier to source than for newer brands. Inspect the bag seams each fall and keep the drive tensioned. It is the right pick for an acre of mixed leaves with a capable lawn tractor.
products.bestFor: Acre-size lots with mixed leaves and a capable tractor.
pros: Published 5.6 to 1 brush ratio keeps pickup consistent
28 cu ft flow-through bag fills evenly
cons: Largest bag adds weight for small tractors
Needs a firm bag seam check each season

products.name: Garvee 44-Inch Tow Sweeper 26 cu ft Folding
products.description:
Garvee builds this sweeper around a folding frame and a widened interface between the metal housing and the brush, which increases the contact the bristles make with the ground. Folding is a practical feature if your shed is tight, because a sweeper is bulky and rarely stored well.

Against the Agri-Fab at 28 cu ft, the Garvee holds 26, a small gap in capacity. Where it differs is documentation: no brush ratio is published, so you are relying on the design description rather than a number. The Petyee uses very similar wording, which suggests a shared platform among these folding models.

In ownership terms, a folding joint is an extra wear point, so check pivot bolts each season. Store with the bag dry and tension on the drive relaxed if the manual allows. It fits owners who care about storage footprint more than brand heritage.
products.bestFor: Tight sheds where a folding frame saves space.
pros: 26 cu ft hopper is close to the largest
Widened brush interface adds ground contact
cons: Newer brand with thinner parts history

products.name: CuisinAid 44-Inch Tow Sweeper 28 cu ft Lever Height
products.description:
CuisinAid matches the Agri-Fab hopper at 28 cu ft using a non-woven fabric bag and gives you a manual lever to raise or lower the brushes. The enlarged contact area between the metal housing and the brush is its mechanical selling point.

The difference from the Agri-Fab is information and bag type. The Agri-Fab states a 5.6 to 1 ratio and a flow-through fill; the CuisinAid lists neither, so you are buying a similar capacity on a less-documented design. If volume matters and budget is tight, it is a reasonable alternative.

Non-woven fabric bags clog with fine dust and debris over time, so shake and rinse yours after use and let it dry fully. Check the lever pivot for slop and the hitch bracket before towing. It suits owners who want 28 cu ft and are comfortable verifying details themselves.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want 28 cu ft without the premium brand.
pros: 28 cu ft hopper matches the largest here
Manual lever changes height without tools
Non-woven bag shrugs off light moisture
cons: No published brush ratio or flow-through fill
Non-woven bag can clog with fine dust

products.name: Petyee 44-Inch Tow Sweeper Folding Heavy Duty
products.description:
Petyee advertises a folding design and a widened metal-to-brush interface, much like the Garvee. The brush height is adjustable and it connects to a lawn tractor. The listing emphasizes heavy duty construction and powerful spinning brushes.

The weak point is data. No hopper volume appears in the listing, while the Garvee states 26 cu ft and the Agri-Fab 28 cu ft. Without a number, you are guessing at capacity, so confirm it with the seller before ordering. It earns a spot because the folding layout genuinely helps with storage.

Expect the same upkeep as the folding Garvee: check fold pivots and fasteners, empty and dry the bag, and store it indoors. It fits a buyer who prioritizes storage and will verify the details before purchase.
products.bestFor: Buyers short on storage who will verify capacity first.
pros: Widened brush interface adds ground contact
Connects to a standard lawn tractor
cons: Hopper volume not stated in the listing

products.name: Towallmark 44-Inch Tow Sweeper 26 cu ft Foldable
products.description:
Towallmark pairs a 26 cu ft non-woven bag with a fold-away frame and a lever that adjusts the brush height without tools. It is aimed at buyers who sweep different surfaces and want quick changes between lawn and paving.

It matches the Garvee on capacity and folding but adds an explicit lever description. Compared with the Agri-Fab, you lose the published brush ratio and flow-through bag, and you trade a bit of capacity for storage savings. The fold hinge is the part to inspect.

Ownership is routine: dry the bag, check the lever and pivots, and keep fasteners snug. It suits someone who wants the Garvee features with a clearly described lever.
products.bestFor: Switching often between lawn and hard surfaces.
cons: Non-woven bag clogs with fine dust
Fold hinge is a wear point

products.name: IDEALHOUSE 44-Inch Tow Sweeper 26 cu ft Rope Dump
products.description:
IDEALHOUSE offers a 26 cu ft non-woven hopper, a lever for tool-free brush height and a rope dump on a 44 inch path. Its reinforced metal-to-brush interface is the same design theme as the Garvee and Towallmark.

The real difference is the rope dump, which lets you empty without leaving the seat, as the Agri-Fab does with its seat dump. The IDEALHOUSE lacks a brush ratio and flow-through fill, so treat it as a straightforward capacity option rather than a performance leader.

Check the rope for fraying and the lever for play. Rinse and dry the bag, and store the unit under cover. It fits buyers who want rope dumping with 26 cu ft.
products.bestFor: Seat-dump convenience with a 26 cu ft bag.
pros: Rope dump from the tractor seat
cons: No flow-through bag or brush ratio
Rope struggles with packed wet loads

buyingCriteria.explanation: The ratio sets how fast the brushes spin compared with the wheels. The Agri-Fab 44-inch publishes 5.6 to 1, meaning acceptable brush speed even at slow tractor speeds. Most other listings here, including the Garvee and CuisinAid, skip it. A missing number is not proof of a poor design, but it means you cannot compare. Test it by watching leaves lift at your usual speed; if they roll ahead of the brush, you are driving too slowly for that ratio.

Hoppers here run from 26 cu ft on the Garvee to 28 cu ft on the Agri-Fab and CuisinAid. A full bag of damp leaves is heavy, and a small lawn tractor on a slope can stall. The mistake is assuming a bigger bag always helps. Match bag size to your tractor's drawbar capacity. Weigh a sample bag of your own leaves if you can, because a cubic foot of damp oak leaves is several times heavier than a cubic foot of dry grass clippings.

The Garvee, Petyee and Towallmark fold for storage, while the Agri-Fab does not. A fold joint adds a pivot that can loosen or wear, so check bolts each season. Fold if your shed is tight, fixed if you tow often over rough ground. A folding unit like the Garvee also hangs on a shed wall, which keeps the bag and brushes off a damp floor.

A lever like the CuisinAid or Towallmark changes height without tools, which helps when you sweep lawn then driveway. Brushes should just touch grass tips. Too low drags the bristles and strains the tow vehicle. Check the lever for a locking notch, since a lever that slips under vibration drops the brush to the ground and burns bristles.

The Agri-Fab uses a flow-through bag that fills evenly, while others use a non-woven bag that can clog with fine dust. Clogging reduces airflow and fill efficiency, so shake out the bag after each use. Fine dust is the enemy, so rap the bag on a post after every use and let it air dry.

Seat dumping saves climbing on and off. The Agri-Fab and IDEALHOUSE both offer it, but a thin rope strains with packed wet loads. Check the rope length and attachment point before towing. If the rope is too short to reach from the seat, add a longer cord before the first pull.

specDecoder.meaning: The brush path, not the overall machine width. The frame and wheels extend beyond the swept strip.
specDecoder.watchFor: Measure gates against the frame width, not the 44 inch figure, on every sweeper here. Allow for the frame when you plan your lane.

specDecoder.meaning: Volume of the inflated bag. Wet leaves and packing cut usable volume.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Petyee lists no volume at all, while the Agri-Fab states 28 cu ft. Ask the seller when a figure is missing.

specDecoder.meaning: Brush turns per wheel turn. Higher means faster brushes at any ground speed.
specDecoder.watchFor: Only the Agri-Fab states it, at 5.6 to 1.

specDecoder.meaning: Air exits through the fabric as debris enters, so the bag fills evenly.
specDecoder.watchFor: Only the Agri-Fab lists this among the picks here.

specDecoder.meaning: A broader mounting between housing and brush that reduces flex and adds ground contact.
specDecoder.watchFor: Garvee, Petyee, Towallmark and IDEALHOUSE use similar wording, so verify it is real on your unit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Brush speed information
howWeEvaluated.description: We favored sweepers that publish a brush-to-wheel ratio, because it tells you how the brushes will behave at mower speed. Only the Agri-Fab 44-inch states 5.6 to 1. Missing data counted against others. We also asked what each listing leaves out.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity relative to tow load
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared hoppers from 26 to 28 cu ft and considered what a full bag demands from the tow vehicle. We did not reward size alone.

howWeEvaluated.title: Storage and frame design
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at folding frames on the Garvee, Petyee and Towallmark versus the fixed Agri-Fab. Folding scored for storage but lost points for extra wear joints.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: Based on common complaints, we weighed short dump ropes, clogging bags and loose hardware. Wear patterns repeat across brands, which makes them useful when specs are thin.

howWeEvaluated.title: Parts support
howWeEvaluated.description: We scored established attachment makers above new listings, since replacement bags and brushes matter by year three.

cards.label: Folding
cards.text: The Garvee, Petyee and Towallmark fold for storage. You gain shed space and give up a little rigidity at the hinge.

cards.label: Fixed
cards.text: The Agri-Fab and CuisinAid keep a fixed frame. They store bulkier but tow with less hinge wear.

howToChoose.note: Fold if storage is tight, fixed if you tow over rough ground.

rows: Flow-through fill from back to front

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A brush speed that stays high at tractor pace and a bag that fills evenly. Low brush speed leaves cones behind.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Agri-Fab 44-inch lists pinecones and clippings and publishes 5.6 to 1, so it is the pick. The Garvee is the fallback with its widened interface.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have over an acre and a capable tractor. The Agri-Fab 44-inch justifies its tier with a documented ratio and parts support.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Your lot is moderate and you can verify specs yourself. The CuisinAid 44-inch or Garvee 44-inch gives similar volume for less.

maintenance.task: Shake out and dry the hopper bag
maintenance.why: Non-woven bags clog with fine dust. A damp bag mildews and weakens at the seams. Do this before storage as well as after each session.
Worn bristles stop touching turf at the lowest height. Replace before pickup drops.
Hinges and bolts loosen with vibration. Loose hinges let the brush drift.
A frayed rope fails under a packed load. A sloppy lever loses height setting. Replace a worn cord early because it is cheap.
A worn bracket can fail on a sharp turn. Replace bent pins at once.

faq.a: It cuts passes slightly and usually comes with a larger bag. It is a better fit for acre-size lots, but needs a gate wide enough for the frame. Measure your narrowest gate first.
The Agri-Fab sits at the high end of this group, and the CuisinAid and Garvee sit lower. Spend more for documented specs and parts support.
The frame outlasts the bag and bristles. Expect to replace both by year three with regular use. Brush wear is cheap to fix when parts exist.

faq.q: Does 28 cu ft pick up more than 26 cu ft?
faq.a: No. Capacity only changes how often you dump. Pickup depends on brush speed and height.

faq.q: Can a small tractor pull a 44 inch sweeper?
faq.a: Yes when the bag is not packed with wet leaves. A full 28 cu ft bag can overload a light tractor on a slope. Sweep when the grass is dry and the tires have traction.
They add a hinge, which is a wear point. Check the bolts regularly and they hold up fine for most lots. A fold joint needs only a wrench and a few minutes each season.
